papers.title: On the Limits of a Space-Time Description and the Physical Meaning of Phase Space in a Nonlocal Continuum
papers.abstract: In a previous paper we derived an uncertainty relation for nonlocal fields by showing that the physical localization width in nonlocal quantum field theory is broadened by the response kernel generated from the entire-function regulator. In this follow up we will reinterpret that result as just the position-sector limit of a more symmetric statement as we did not take into account the inherent nonlocality of momentum. We find and we prove under normalized, centered response kernels for both position and momentum the variance laws and derive the corresponding nonlocal phase-space uncertainty relation. The result still preserves the conclusions of the original paper all while strengthening the interpretation as nonlocal quantum field theory implies not merely a minimal measurable length, but a finite phase-space cell. We also explore experimental routes to test the theory.

papers.title: Revisiting self-interacting dark matter with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation observations
papers.abstract: We revisit self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), originally proposed to resolve small-scale CDM problems and drive late-time cosmic acceleration. Using latest DESI BAO, Pantheon+/DESY5 type Ia supernova, and cosmic chronometer Hubble data, we constrain three representative SIDM scenarios including creation and annihilation. We focus on the annihilation of dark matter particles in model SIDM1; our findings indicate the effective annihilation cross section is $\log_{10}(\kappa C_1)=-4.32$ (with an upper limit of $\log_{10}(\kappa C_1)=-3.90$). For the SIDM2 model, the SIDM fluid behaves similarly to a dark energy component with a mildly dynamical equation of state ($w_{\rm{SIDM}}=-0.82 \pm 0.04$). We also quantitatively discuss the dark matter self-interactions in a more general SIDM model (SIDM3), which reveals a strong correlation between the annihilation cross section and equation of state of dark matter. For the three SIDM models, the measured Hubble constant agrees with that derived from the recent Planck 2018 results; both are inconsistent with the results of the SH0ES collaboration, who report a significantly higher $H_0$ value. The Bayesian evidence indicates that SIDM2 and SIDM3 are more supported by the available observational data than the concordance standard $\Lambda$CDM. Furthermore, the cosmological constraints on the effective annihilation parameter can be translated into bounds on the velocity-averaged annihilation cross section and the self-interaction cross section per unit mass. While low-redshift data alone imply a relatively large cross section, the inclusion of cosmic microwave background distance priors significantly tightens the constraint at cluster-scale velocities, highlighting the necessity of a velocity-dependent cross section to reconcile cosmological and astrophysical observations.

papers.title: Towards a General Theory of GPS Inter-Satellite Communications Between Moving Satellites on Arbitrary Space Trajectories, Accounting for General Relativity Effects
papers.abstract: In previous publications it has been shown that it is possible to calculate (in terms of zero and higher order elliptic integrals) the propagation time of a signal, emitted by a satellite, moving along a plane (or space-determined) Kepler orbit. 2. By means of a method of intersecting null cones, the propagation time was found for the case, when the signal is intercepted by a second satellite. The present paper has the purpose to generalize the above approach for satellites, exchanging signals and moving along arbitrary space trajectories. Previously, the important physical notions of space-time distance and geodesic distance (only positive and greater than the Euclidean distance) have been introduced. It will be shown that these notions can be introduced also for the case of general motion of the satellites, and more importantly, they have the same physical meaning. A generalization of the s. c. ranging equation for the case of a curved space-time has been proposed. It has been proved that the geodesic distances of propagation of the signal in the forward and in the backward directions are not equal. The physical reason is hidden in the non-inertial reference systems of motion of the two satellites. Thus, signal propagation in non-inertial systems is an irreversible process, meaning that the propagation times in the two directions is different. A mathematical model has been created for the forward and subsequent backward propagation of the signal between two moving satellites in a gravitational field. Such a general theory of inter-satellite communications is the first step towards constructing a modern theory for optimal propagation of signals in an integrated dense satellite communication network systems, such as the current 6G and future 7G systems.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Finslerian Cosmological Dark Energy Model
papers.abstract: Modified extensions of the standard cosmological models often introduce complex parameter degeneracies that severely impact sampling convergence of the parameter space while analyzing the model observationally. In this work, we present an accelerated Bayesian inference technique using a Heteroscedastic Deep Ensemble with Monte Carlo Dropout incorporating distance-gated local residual corrections to emulate complex likelihood surfaces and avoid extrapolation beyond the trained region. We demonstrate this methodology on a unified dark energy cosmological model equipped with Finsler geometry. The model is studied using the recent observational datasets, including Cosmic Chronometers (CC), Pantheon$+$SH$0$ES, and DESI DR$2$ BAO measurements. While the conventional sampling procedure struggles with slow mixing of parameter chains ($\tau_{max}=1578.3$), the neural network, specially trained densely in high likelihood regions, yields converged and highly resolved posterior distributions of the model parameters without significantly compromising the minimum chi-square value. We further discuss the results for physical inferences and also compare the present dark energy model with $\Lambda\text{CDM}$ statistically using AIC and BIC.

papers.title: Is the Kaniadakis deformation of holographic dark energy detectable? A non-flat analysis with DESI DR2, cosmic chronometers and Pantheon+SH0ES
papers.abstract: Kaniadakis entropy deforms the horizon entropy through a single parameter $K$, and the holographic dark energy built on it (KHDE) reduces to the standard model as $K\to0$. We ask whether current data can detect this deformation when spatial curvature is free and no cosmic-microwave-background calibration is assumed. Combining Pantheon+SH0ES supernovae, with the absolute magnitude fitted against the Cepheid calibrators, 32 cosmic-chronometer measurements of $H(z)$ and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations with a free sound horizon, we find that non-flat KHDE fits the data as well as flat $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\chi^2=-2.1$ for three additional parameters) but leaves $K$ unconstrained: the profile $\chi^2$ changes by only $0.47$ between $K=0$ and its best value, and the bound $K<0.67$ (95%) reflects the validity domain of the model rather than the data. Information criteria therefore prefer $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\mathrm{AIC}=+3.9$, $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=+20.2$). The joint fit gives $\Omega_{k0}=0.012\pm0.045$, three times tighter than supernovae alone, $H_0=72.04\pm0.85\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $r_d=139.34\pm1.76\,\mathrm{Mpc}$; chronometers and DESI alone prefer $H_0=68.17\pm1.93$, $2.4\sigma$ below the supernova value. In the fitted model, acceleration begins at $z_t=0.66\pm0.03$; a model-independent neural-network reconstruction of $H(z)$ from the chronometers gives a present-day deceleration parameter $q_0=-0.46\pm0.14$, consistent with the model. We also identify three analysis requirements which, if ignored, make the deformation numerically invisible, underestimate the $H_0$ uncertainty fourfold, or spuriously reject the model.
